On the other hand the case of the contesting defendants (government) is that the predecessors of the plaintiffs themselves established a Bazar in .39 acre of land of this plot in the year 1939 and as such in R.S. record this .39 acre of land has been duly recorded in the khas khatian of the government 

 5. The trial court accepted this case of the contesting defendant and found that there is a hat in .39 acre of land out of the scheduled land and as such the trial court decreed the suit in part declaring the plaintiffs' title in .61 acre of land out of the schedule 'Ka' land by the judgment and decree data 24.08.2000. Against that judgment and decree the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 227 of 2000 before the District Judge, Brahmanbaria which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the Additional District Judge, Brahmanbaria. That appellate court dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree of the trial court by the judgment and decree dated 17.11.2004. The plaintiffs they, preferred the above mentioned civil revision before the High Court Division and obtained rule. A Single Bench of the High Court Division, upon hearing the learned Counsel of both the parties and examining the materials on record made that rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order. The High Court Division observed that admittedly both the C.S. and S.A. records of the suit land stood in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs and that there is no evidence to prove that there is any hat and bazar in this land as described in schedule `Ka' to the plaint. The High Court Division, on scrutiny of the evidence, both oral and documentary, adduced by both the parties, found that there was a not in the waqf property i.e. .18 acre of land of the suit plot which supports the plaintiffs' case that the alleged hat was illegally and forcibly established in the waqf land, but not in their suit land. The High Court Division also considered the legal aspect of the matter and opined that if the defence case that the predecessors of the plaintiffs established the hat in the suit land in the year 1939 were true than in S.A. khatian this land ought to have been recorded as hat and bazar in the name of the government, but since in S.A. khatian, admittedly, the suit land has been recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs also paid rent for the said land and got rent receipts the defendant's claim is not acceptable. The High Court Division observed also that though the suit land has been recorded in the name of government in R.S. khatian, but the defendant could not adduce any evidence to prove the basis of this recording of the suit land. 

 6. On careful consideration of the evidence on record including the Advocate Commissioner's report, the proceeding under Waqf Act in respect of the waqf land the High Court Division calm to the conclusion that though .39 acre of land of the suit plot has been recorded in the name of government in khatian only, but there is nothing to prove that this land vested in the government by operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The High Court Division pointed out also that since in C.S. and also in S.A. khatian the suit land has been recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs and since there is nothing to prove that there is an established old hat or bazar in the suit land the R.S. khatian only could not prove at all that there is actually any old hat and bazar in the suit land and as such it vested in the government according to the provision of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.
